html:
SMTO-HTTP-0019 — A saved web service connection has settings SMTO can't use

GUID: 9d59d817-0e33-42e4-919f-8b842780324e
Slug: http-profile-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO checked the settings of a saved web service connection and found one that is missing, conflicts with another, or isn't supported, so it didn't use the connection.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and select the connection SMTO used. Make sure it is an HTTP connection and that Base URL and the Authentication fields are filled in. SMTO can't use a connection that is missing required details or isn't an HTTP connection.
  2. For OAuth sign-in, fill in Token endpoint or Issuer. For Browser authorization, also fill Authorization endpoint and set Redirect URI to SMTO's web address followed by /api/agent/http/oauth/callback. SMTO only accepts OAuth sign-ins that return to that exact address.
  3. Under Custom certificate authority, set CA source to either Certificate PEM or File on Gateway. Under Client certificate, give both the certificate and its key. SMTO rejects a connection that mixes both certificate sources or has a certificate without its key.
  4. Select Save, then select Test connection before asking SMTO to use the connection again. The test confirms the corrected settings work before the task depends on them.

What success looks like

  • Test connection succeeds and SMTO uses the connection without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste passwords, client secrets or tokens into the conversation or the error report; keep them only in Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An HTTP profile, authentication recipe or OAuth discovery document failed validation (for example a missing OAuth endpoint, wrong redirect URI, conflicting certificate settings, or a parameter that is not an HTTP connection).

What this means

  • A typed profile, authentication recipe, OAuth discovery document or related normalization fails its schema or supported configuration checks; a pre-dispatch wrapper may also map an unexpected exception here. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A typed profile, authentication recipe, OAuth discovery document or related normalization fails its schema or supported configuration checks; a pre-dispatch wrapper may also map an unexpected exception here.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe rejected field names, profile type and discovery issuer/endpoint checks; preserve an unexpected exception as a possible runtime defect.

How to fix it

  • Read the message in Technical details; it names the failed check, such as OAuth requiring token_endpoint or issuer, redirect_uri not being exactly the Server's /api/agent/http/oauth/callback URL, a missing authorization or device endpoint, an issuer discovery mismatch, conflicting CA or client-certificate settings, an auth endpoint outside allowed_origins, or a parameter whose profile_type is not http_connection. Correct that field in the Parameter Store HTTP profile and run Test connection; if no field violation is named, keep the occurrence details for runtime diagnosis.
  • Correct the identified typed-profile violation; if no field violation is established, retain the occurrence details for runtime diagnosis.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The current intended profile validates and the supported connection test passes.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
